observations: DEVICE / TARGET CONFIRMED — Opened by confirming the target rather than assuming it: `adb -s R58MB3SGZVL shell getprop ro.product.model` reads SM-A405FM, `ro.build.version.release` reads 11 and `ro.build.version.sdk` reads 30. Every adb command in this record carries `-s R58MB3SGZVL`; only one device was addressed.

ARTIFACT VERIFIED, INSTALLED, AND ITS INSTALLED BYTES HASHED — The built artifact and the installed base.apk are byte-identical on both size and sha256 (19985218 bytes; ab15d769cc6e0c8079d3ab3e63fbbf39ee870fe0cd1f8b168868ea019a86ea9e), read independently by Get-FileHash on the host and `sha256sum` on the phone. `dumpsys package` reads DEBUGGABLE, which is what let this run read the app's own private files. The previous record could not do this: the phone then held the RELEASE artifact, so `run-as` answered 'package not debuggable' and the app's own disk state was unreadable. The app's data was cleared with `pm clear com.gexetr.unitwalk.debug` first so the first-run state would be real.

OBSERVATION 1 / THE CAMERA IS A REAL RUNTIME PERMISSION, NOT A SILENT PROMPT — Tapping 'Add photo' on the room detail raised the system permission dialog 'Allow UnitWalk to take pictures and record video' with 'While using the app', 'Only this time' and 'Don't allow' (bounds read from the dump), and `dumpsys activity activities` read mResumedActivity= com.google.android.permissioncontroller/.GrantPermissionsActivity. On a freshly cleared install the permission had never been granted, so the CAMERA permission in the manifest is actually exercised by this path rather than merely declared.

OBSERVATION 2 / THE CAMERA SHUTTER AND THE RETURN LEG — Granting 'While using the app' handed the screen to the system camera: mResumedActivity= com.sec.android.app.camera/.Camera, whose own hierarchy reads 'Take picture' as a content-desc'd ImageButton, plus 'Wide', 'Normal', 'Flash', 'Timer', 'Ratio', 'Effects' and 'Switch to rear camera'. No control carries a text label, so the shutter was fired with `input keyevent 27` (KEYCODE_CAMERA), which is what the camera app itself exposes. The result was the review screen (content-desc 'Image viewer' with 'Retry' and 'OK'); tapping 'OK' returned mResumedActivity= com.gexetr.unitwalk.debug/.MainActivity, and the room then carried a photo node with content-desc photo-916eb7ce-00b9-4460-8150-8938e72da59d. The app's own store confirms it: files/photos/photo-916eb7ce-00b9-4460-8150-8938e72da59d.jpg at 1806002 bytes with "source":"CAMERA" in walk-state.json. This closes the previous record's first NOT DRIVEN item; the gallery route was already driven there, so both doors into a room are now measured.

OBSERVATION 3 / THE CONDITION IS READ FROM STATE, NOT FROM A COLOUR — The Condition row renders four chips; of the nodes carrying checkable=true exactly one carries checked=true and it is the one whose text is 'Worn' (Good, Damaged and Missing all read checked=false). The finished report later prints condition 'Worn' for that room, so the chip the hierarchy said was selected is the value the document carries.

OBSERVATION 4 / THE NOTE IS WRITTEN AS YOU TYPE, NOT ONLY ON BLUR — This is the measurement the previous record did not make. The note field is the EditText whose own subtree contains a text node reading exactly 'Note' (this run addressed it by that placeholder after an earlier pass typed into the 'Room name' field, which is a different control, and measured nothing about the note). 'Cracked tile near the sink' was typed, and while the field still held focus `run-as ... cat files/walk-state.json` ALREADY carried that string — the draft is on disk before the field is left. Separately, the same test was run against the previous revision with the text appended and the process killed with the field still dirty: the disk carried the appended sentence and the relaunched app read it back into the field, so the durability does not depend on a blur, a Next tap or a clean exit. This is the property the promise 'crash-safe-photo-draft' names and that the Property360 and Yardi reviews say their apps lost.

OBSERVATION 5 / PROCESS DEATH, OBSERVED AT THE PROCESS LEVEL — `pidof com.gexetr.unitwalk.debug` reads a live pid (30561), `am force-stop` is issued, and the same command then returns nothing at all — the process is gone, not merely backgrounded. Relaunching with `monkey -p ... -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1` yields a new pid and the app comes back with its data: files/walk-state.json still carries the unit 'Flat 3B', the finished MOVE_IN walk, the room 'Kitchen', the note and the CAMERA photo, and the walk detail re-renders them. The previous record listed process-death restore as NOT DRIVEN and said the walk survived 'because the app stayed alive'; this run kills it and the data survives anyway.

OBSERVATION 6 / THE INTERRUPTED DESTINATION IS RESTORED — Twice in this run the app was force-stopped while a walk was open, and on relaunch it did not return to the unit list: it reopened on the walk screen reading 'Kitchen / 1 of 1 / 1 photos in this walk / Draft'. That is the SavedStateHandle half of the promise — the position, not just the data, is durable — and it was observed without being asked for, because the driver expected the unit list and the app was already further in.

OBSERVATION 7 / THE WALK FINISHES AND THE COMPARISON RENDERS — 'Finish room' returned the overview reading 'Kitchen / <note> / 1 photos / Worn', and 'Finish walk' opened the comparison as 'Move-in vs move-out / Flat 3B / Move-in / No prior report' with the sentence 'There is no prior move-in report for this unit, so only the current walk is shown. No baseline has been invented.' and 'Each condition is shown as a word and a shape, never by colour alone.' The per-room block reads 'Kitchen / Move-in / No prior report' above 'Move-out / Worn' beside the four-chip 'Room condition' row and a 'Note for this room' field. The sealed PDF later carries the same unit and the same condition, so the comparison the user sees and the document they keep agree.

OBSERVATION 8 / THE REPORT SURFACE — 'Open the report' produced 'Flat 3B / Signed condition report' with the counts the walk actually holds ('1 Rooms / 1 Photos / 1 Differences / 0 Signatures'), the file name report-walk-caf013c9-e2b8-4091-b2d7-ddfa30e26fa8.pdf and the byte size 204012, and both export controls present: 'Share the PDF' and 'Save a copy'. `run-as ... ls -l files/reports` lists that exact file at 204012 bytes, so the size on screen is the size on disk.

OBSERVATION 9 / BOTH data_out CONTROLS ARE REALLY PRESSED — The previous record read their enabled state and explicitly did not tap them; this run taps both. 'Share the PDF' moved mResumedActivity to android/com.android.internal.app.ChooserActivity whose own hierarchy names the file report-walk-caf013c9-e2b8-4091-b2d7-ddfa30e26fa8 and offers real targets (Telegram, Gmail, Quick Share), which is an ACTION_SEND reaching the system chooser. The chooser was then dismissed with system back and nothing was sent. 'Save a copy' moved mResumedActivity to com.google.android.documentsui/com.android.documentsui.picker.PickActivity in Downloads with the suggested file name Flat_3B.pdf; tapping SAVE wrote /sdcard/Download/Flat_3B.pdf at 203698 bytes — byte-for-byte the size the report screen had declared for that walk — and the file was then removed and `ls /sdcard/Download` confirmed back to the four pre-existing user files. So both the share sheet and the SAF create-document path are measured, and the report reaches external storage only because a human chose a destination.

OBSERVATION 10 / THE FREE-TIER PDF CARRIES THE WATERMARK, MEASURED FROM THE BYTES ON THIS REVISION — The phone's copy and the local copy hash identically (a418977cbb8b9921be03f3e13df2000b71e46d79193a00405696beb701878c00) and the local header is b'%PDF-1.4', so the file inspected is the file the app wrote. Android's PdfDocument draws text as subset-font glyph codes, so a literal needle search in the raw bytes sees none of it — the raw streams contain 5997 printable ASCII runs and none of them is a word of the report. The text was therefore rebuilt from the document itself: each font's own ToUnicode CMap was decoded through the page's /Fn resource map and the content streams' 333 Tj operands were mapped through it. The rebuilt text begins 'FREE PREVIEWUnlock UnitWalk to remove this stamp' and continues 'Flat 3BWalk: Move-inStarted: 2026-10-06T18:29:37.533ZFinished: 2026-10-06T18:36:04.288ZRooms: 1 Photos: 1Rooms1. Kitchen Condition: Worn Cracked tile near the sinkand the tap is loose Photos: photo-916eb7ce-...jpgDifferences- WornSignaturesNot signed.' The watermark, the unit, the room, the condition the chip reported, the note typed under process-death test, the CAMERA photo's file name and the unsigned state are all present. What this does NOT measure is the stamp's visual prominence (angle, translucency, size) — only that the watermark glyphs are drawn ahead of the body.

OBSERVATION 11 / A DRIVER ERROR, AND WHY IT DID NOT COMPOUND — An early navigation helper fell back to matching the substring 'Move-in' and tapped the section header rather than the button, creating a second, empty MOVE_IN draft beside the finished walk; the state file then held two walks. Later, a tap issued while the Units list was re-composing read a stale list ('Flat' with 'No move-in baseline yet') while the disk held 'Flat 3B' with a finished baseline; two settled re-reads agreed with the disk and with each other, and a full `run-as ... find . -type f` showed files/walk-state.json is the only store, so the stale frame was a recomposition artefact and not a second source of truth or a data loss. Both are recorded because they are the class of error the device rule warns about: a tap point copied from an earlier frame, or a single dump trusted as the state of the app. Every later tap in this run came from a dump of the frame it was about to change.

NOT DRIVEN, NAMED PLAINLY — (1) No purchase was made or attempted: 'Unlock for $9.99' and 'Restore purchase' were not tapped, so the owned state remains unobserved and every paywall observation here is about the NOT-OWNED state. (2) The share sheet's targets were not used: the chooser was dismissed with back, so 'the PDF reached another app' is not claimed, only that the system chooser received it. (3) Language was not switched this run; the Settings surface and the in-app privacy policy opener were measured in the previous run and are not re-claimed here. (4) Tablet, foldable, landscape and 7-inch/10-inch layouts were not driven — this run is one phone, SM-A405FM at 1080x2340, portrait only. (5) Dark mode and the 'Use wallpaper colours' preference were not toggled. (6) The unit 'Rename' and 'Delete' flows and 'Delete this walk' were not driven. (7) Only one room was walked and only one condition was set, so a multi-room walk's comparison arithmetic is measured by the JVM suite rather than on the phone. (8) The camera was driven once; the gallery/photo-picker route was driven in the previous run and is not re-claimed here.

STATE LEFT ON THE PHONE — The debug package is installed, running (pidof reads 3688) and showing the walk's report screen; its data holds the unit, the finished walk, the note, the CAMERA photo and both PDFs. The release package com.gexetr.unitwalk, also installed, was neither launched nor modified. No device-wide setting was changed, no locale was set, and no package the factory did not install was uninstalled or had its data cleared. This run's own /sdcard temporaries were removed, and so were ~90 dump files earlier passes had left in /sdcard; /sdcard/Download holds only its four pre-existing files.

findings.previouslyReported: Not reported as a finding, because no earlier run pressed the shutter: the camera was listed as NOT DRIVEN, and the revision under test was changed specifically to make it work.
findings.observedNow: MEASURED, both ways. The defect this revision fixes: on a clean install files/reports/ did not exist, so FileProvider could not create the camera's destination file and a shutter press produced no photo while reporting nothing. The fix is in ui/walk/PhotoUris.kt, whose captureFile() now ends with .also { it.parentFile?.mkdirs() }. On this run the whole path works from a freshly cleared install: the permission dialog appears, the camera opens, KEYCODE_CAMERA fires the shutter, 'OK' returns to the app, and the room gains photo-916eb7ce-00b9-4460-8150-8938e72da59d — which `run-as ... ls -l` confirms is a real 1806002-byte file with "source":"CAMERA" in walk-state.json, and whose name the finished PDF prints. files/reports/ now exists and holds both PDFs the run produced.
findings.whyItMatters: A camera button that silently does nothing is the worst shape of this defect: the user has already framed and taken the shot, and the app reports no error. It is the same class as the durability failures this slot's promise is written against.

findings.screen: walk screen, room detail, note field, against a process kill
findings.previouslyReported: Not previously reported. It was raised as a question this run was written to answer: the promise says a kill cannot lose work, and a draft written only when the field loses focus would make that false for exactly the case the user is most likely to be in.
findings.observedNow: The negative observation was NOT found, and that is the result. With text typed into the note field and the field still focused, `run-as ... cat files/walk-state.json` already carried the typed sentence, and an earlier pass that appended text and force-stopped without blurring found the appended sentence both on disk and re-rendered in the field after relaunch. The finished PDF written afterwards contains that same note text. So the write is not gated on blur, Next or a clean exit.
findings.whyItMatters: This is the promise's sharpest case. If the draft were committed only on blur, a kill while typing would lose exactly the sentence the user was in the middle of, and the whole differentiator against Property360 and Yardi would be unproven for the common case rather than the tidy one.
